Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $E$ denote the expression in the question. Recognize the expanded perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(\cos^2\left(67.5^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(67.5^\circ\right)\right)^2
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the cosine double-angle identity:

$$
\cos^2\left(x\right)-\sin^2\left(x\right)=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute the angle and evaluate the standard-angle cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\cos^2\left(67.5^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(67.5^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(2\cdot 67.5^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(135^\circ\right) \\
&= -\cos\left(45^\circ\right) \\
&= -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, square the value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^2 \\
&= \frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $E$ denote the expression in the question. Recognize the expanded perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(\cos^2\left(45^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(45^\circ\right)\right)^2
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the cosine double-angle identity:

$$
\cos^2\left(x\right)-\sin^2\left(x\right)=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute the angle and evaluate the standard-angle cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\cos^2\left(45^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(45^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(2\cdot 45^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(90^\circ\right) \\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, square the value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(0\right)^2 \\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $E$ denote the expression in the question. Recognize the expanded perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(\cos^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)-\sin^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)\right)^2
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the cosine double-angle identity:

$$
\cos^2\left(x\right)-\sin^2\left(x\right)=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute the angle and evaluate the standard-angle cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\cos^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)-\sin^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}\right) \\
&= \cos\left(2\cdot \frac{5\pi}{12}\right) \\
&= \cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) \\
&= -\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\
&= -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, square the value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 \\
&= \frac{3}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$
